Subject: Quick follow-up: pricing metrics (tokens vs characters vs requests)

Hi Samir -

Thanks again for the call today - really helpful to understand the integration pattern and the three main flows you talked about (clinical note summarization, triage assistant, and patient Q&A). Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can put together a clean pricing estimate:

Recap (from our call):
- Clinical notes: ~200K docs/month, average raw note length ~1,200 characters, we expect to send the full note + short system prompt, average model response ~150 tokens.
- Triage assistant: ~60K interactions/month, average prompt ~250 characters, expected response ~80 tokens.
- Patient Q&A: ~500K lightweight requests/month, short prompts (~50 chars), responses ~20-40 tokens.

Primary ask: can you confirm expected monthly request counts and whether the figures above are pro forma or conservative? Specifically, we need: requests/month, average prompt length (chars), and average response length (tokens).

Common pricing confusion we see (so you know what we'll include in the estimate):
- Tokens vs characters vs requests: Redwood bills on tokens (input + output) - characters are a useful proxy for estimating tokens but are not the billed metric. Requests = number of API calls; tokens = billed unit.
- Prompt caching vs billed tokens: prompt (prefix) caching reduces tokens sent to the model and therefore reduces billed tokens if the same prompt/prefix is reused exactly. However, dynamic parts (user text) are still billed. Caching helps most when you have large static system prompts / instruction templates.

To help align on unit economics, do you have a target budget or target $/1M tokens you want to hit? For rough context, I'll include a few pricing bands in our proposal (e.g., $100, $200, $300 per 1M tokens) and show the projected monthly cost under each band so the finance team can pick.

I've attached a short pricing one-pager and a worksheet (blank) so you can paste expected volumes; I'll turn it into a formal proposal.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm the volumes/averages above (requests/month, avg prompt chars, avg response tokens).
2) If you have any existing monthly token estimates from internal tooling, paste them into the attached worksheet.
3) I'll run a model-level cost estimate and send back a short options table (3 tiers) + recommended configuration (batching, caching, and quantization suggestions).

Thanks - happy to hop on another quick call if that helps.

Best,

Hi Samir -

Thanks for the detailed numbers - that helps a lot. Answers inline and a quick unit-economics sketch below.

Caching and billed tokens:
- Short answer: Redwood bills on tokens (input + output) that are actually sent to the model. If you have an exact cached prefix (e.g., a static 400-char system prompt) and Redwood serves the call from an internal cache so that prefix is not re-sent to the model, those cached tokens are not billed on a per-request basis. In practice:
  - If prefix is identical and we fully cache it: only dynamic user tokens + model response tokens are billed.
  - If prefix is templated but has small dynamic fields (e.g., patient ID), the dynamic portion is billed.
  - Caching benefits are most material when the static prompt is large relative to dynamic user text.

Requests vs tokens for the proposal:
- Yes, please provide token estimates (input+output) if possible - that's what we'll use for the formal cost projection. If you can only provide characters, we'll convert with a conservative chars->tokens ratio (roughly 4 chars = 1 token for English prose) and call out the conversion assumption in the proposal.

Quick unit economics (using your numbers + your budget target $180 / 1M tokens):
- Clinical notes: estimate tokens/request:
  - Input: ~ (1,150 chars + 400-char static prompt) -> ~ (1550 chars / 4) ≈ 388 input tokens (we'll show a range)
  - Output: 160 tokens
  - Total per request: ~548 tokens
  - Monthly tokens = 180,000 * 548 ≈ 98.6M tokens
  - Monthly cost @ $180 / 1M = 98.6 * $180 ≈ $17,748
- Triage assistant:
  - Input: 300 chars -> ~75 tokens; Output: 90 tokens -> total ~165 tokens/request
  - Monthly tokens = 70,000 * 165 ≈ 11.6M tokens -> Cost ≈ $2,088 @ $180/1M
- Patient Q&A (light):
  - Input: 45 chars -> ~11 tokens; Output: 30 tokens -> total ~41 tokens/request
  - Monthly tokens = 420,000 * 41 ≈ 17.2M tokens -> Cost ≈ $3,096 @ $180/1M

Projected monthly token total ≈ 127.4M tokens -> Projected monthly cost ≈ $22,932 @ $180/1M

Notes and levers to reduce cost:
- Prompt caching: If we can cache the 400-char system prompt for clinical notes, that reduces input tokens to ~288 (1,150 chars => ~288 tokens) - saves ~72 tokens per request. At 180k requests, that's ~13M tokens saved (~$2,340 at $180/1M).
- Batching: for high-throughput flows we can batch small requests to reduce per-request overhead; savings depend on latency SLOs.
- Committed capacity: Reserved/Dedicated pricing can materially lower $/1M tokens - I'll include a reserved capacity option that targets $100–$150 / 1M depending on commit size and model choices.

Next steps:
1) If you can share a CSV export of sample telemetry (even one week's worth), we'll run a quick eval to produce a more precise token estimate and show cached vs uncached scenarios.
2) I'll produce a 3-tier options table (Self-serve hosted, Reserved/dedicated, Enterprise private) with projected monthly costs and recommended levers.

I've updated the attached worksheet with the calculations above - see acme-pricing-proposal.xlsx. Also pulling together a short deck for your director showing the committed-capacity scenarios.

If you're comfortable, I'll include Ben (cc'd) to propose the committed pricing options.

Thanks - happy to jump on a 20-min follow-up if helpful.

Best,
